commands.review_summary:
The branch changes the cron SQLite delivery codec to JSON-encode `delivery.threadId`, decode it on load, and adds cron store regression tests for numeric and string thread IDs.

PR surface: Source +6, Tests +34. Total +40 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection shows current main writes `delivery.threadId` as bare text and the PR head parses that text as JSON on read, which reproduces the remaining upgrade bug for numeric-looking string IDs.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] There is a concrete repair: keep legacy bare-text thread IDs string-typed while preserving the new JSON-scalar format for future writes.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve delivery thread id type across SQLite round-trip
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron job's delivery target can carry a `threadId` that is legitimately either a string or a number (`string | number`). The input schema (`src/cron/delivery-field-schemas.ts`) accepts `z.union([TrimmedNonEmptyStringFieldSchema, z.number().finite()])` and `normalizeCronJobInput` deliberately preserves a numeric thread id. Numeric thread ids are real: for example a Telegram forum/topic id like `1008013`.

The SQLite codec dropped that type. On write it stored the thread id as TEXT via `String(...)`, and on read it handed the raw TEXT column straight back:

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts write path (before)
delivery_thread_id:
  delivery?.threadId === undefined || delivery.threadId === null
    ? null
    : String(delivery.threadId),

// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts read path (before)
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: row.delivery_thread_id } : {}),
```

So a persistence round-trip silently changed the type:

```
INPUT  threadId: 1008013   (number)
LOADED threadId: "1008013" (string)
```

This matters because the reloaded value is what the live delivery path consumes. `rowToCronJob` builds the runtime job from `deliveryFromRow`, and `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` runs the thread id through `normalizeOptionalThreadValue`, which keeps the string-vs-number distinction rather than re-normalizing it. A freshly created in-memory job carries `threadId: 1008013` (number); the same job after a save/reload carries `"1008013"` (string). Identical config produces two different runtime types depending on whether the job came from disk or memory. Telegram's native approval path only sets `messageThreadId` when `typeof threadId === "number"` (`extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`), so a reloaded string-typed topic id is dropped there and the approval posts to the general chat instead of the topic.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix belongs in the codec, which owns encoding and decoding the column. Instead of a lossy `String(...)`, persist the thread id as a JSON scalar so its type is recoverable, and decode it on read. A number round-trips as a number and a string round-trips as a string, including a numeric-looking string such as `"99"` that the doctor legacy repair intentionally produces (`src/commands/doctor/cron/legacy-delivery.ts` normalizes legacy hints with `String(value)`).

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts (after)
delivery_thread_id: serializeJson(delivery?.threadId),
// ...
function threadIdFromColumn(value: string): string | number {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(value) as unknown;
    return typeof parsed === "string" || typeof parsed === "number" ? parsed : value;
  } catch {
    return value;
  }
}
// ...
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: threadIdFromColumn(row.delivery_thread_id) } : {}),
```

`serializeJson` and JSON decoding are the existing pattern in this codec module (`scalar-codec.ts` already exposes `serializeJson`/`parseJsonValue` and this file already JSON-encodes other structured columns). Rows written by earlier releases hold a bare value; the `try/catch` decodes those unchanged (a bare non-JSON id such as `"topic-9"` falls through to the raw string), so no data migration is needed.

## Why this is the right boundary

`bindDeliveryColumns` / `deliveryFromRow` are the canonical writer and reader for the delivery columns, and `rowToCronJob` reconstructs the runtime job from `deliveryFromRow`, so fixing the codec covers the runtime round-trip end to end. The only other writer is `backfillCronJobsFromJobJson` in `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts`, a one-time low-level bootstrap that projects legacy `job_json` rows into the queryable columns; it writes bare text via `textField` (which already only projects string thread ids), and the same tolerant read decodes that output, so it is not a regressed surface. The write path change is an internal storage-format detail on a single column with no user-facing or schema contract; existing rows keep working.

## User Impact

Cron jobs configured with a numeric delivery thread id (for example a Telegram forum/topic id) now deliver to the same thread whether the job is served from memory or reloaded from SQLite. Previously a save/reload silently retyped the id to a string, which downstream paths that require a numeric thread id (such as Telegram native approval delivery) would drop, sending to the general chat instead of the topic. String thread ids are unchanged.

## Evidence

Verification:
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `oxfmt --check src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` -> no errors.
- Added colocated regression tests in `src/cron/store.test.ts` (numeric thread id reloads as a number; non-numeric `"007"` stays a string). vitest could not be run in this checkout (worker startup is killed by the sandbox resource governor); the same save/load assertions are demonstrated live below by driving the real store and the real doctor migration, and the tests run in CI.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a numeric cron delivery thread id (e.g. Telegram topic id 1008013) is retyped to a string by a SQLite save/reload, diverging from the same job held in memory, while a string thread id (including the doctor-repaired "99") must stay a string.
Real environment tested: drove the real `saveCronStore`/`loadCronStore` and `resolveCronDeliveryPlan`, and the real `maybeRepairLegacyCronStore` doctor migration, against a real temp SQLite state DB (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), on pristine main and on the patched tree. Nothing was stubbed: the real codec, the real Kysely store, the real delivery-plan resolver, and the real doctor migration all ran; only the state directory was a throwaway temp dir.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: save jobs with `delivery.threadId` of `1008013` (number), `"007"` (string), and `"99"` (string), then `loadCronStore` and inspect the reloaded thread id plus `resolveCronDeliveryPlan(job).threadId`; and separately run `maybeRepairLegacyCronStore` on a legacy job carrying top-level `threadId: " 99 "` and inspect the repaired `delivery.threadId`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main) store round-trip
numeric loaded threadId: "1008013" string
numeric plan   threadId: "1008013" string
numeric matches in-memory job: false
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
numeric-string loaded threadId: "99" string
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs) store round-trip
numeric loaded threadId: 1008013 number
numeric plan   threadId: 1008013 number
numeric matches in-memory job: true
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
numeric-string loaded threadId: "99" string
# AFTER (this patch) real doctor migration of legacy top-level threadId " 99 "
repaired delivery.threadId: "99" string
delivery.channel: "telegram"
delivery.to: "-1001234567890"
top-level threadId cleared: true
```
Observed result after fix: the reloaded numeric thread id and the resolved delivery-plan thread id come back as the number 1008013 and match the in-memory job, while both the "007" id and the doctor-repaired "99" id stay strings, so the persistence round-trip no longer changes the value's type and the legacy repair output is preserved.
What was not tested: no live Telegram send (the downstream drop is shown by reading `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, not by a live topic post); vitest and full build were not run in this checkout.
